summary: Obfuscated payload hidden in CLI entrypoint executes dynamically constructed code with full require/module access
details: cli.js, the package's declared `bin` entrypoint, prepends an obfuscated IIFE hidden behind roughly 360 leading tab characters to the real deploy-tool CLI dispatch. The blob uses XOR-masked integer constants, unicode-escape identifiers that spell standard Node APIs (`length`, `charAt`, `join`, `substring`, `fromCharCode`), a seeded Fisher–Yates string shuffle (`spin`/`peel`), and resolves `Function.constructor` via `peel[r.substring(0,7)]` to build and immediately invoke a Function from a decoded ~13 KB body. The IIFE is invoked as `(global, require)` and writes `require` and `module` onto `global`, giving the dynamically constructed function arbitrary access to Node's `require`, filesystem, child_process and network APIs. The obfuscated payload is not referenced or disclosed in README.md or CHANGELOG.md, and is placed adjacent to otherwise legitimate-looking Kamal-style deploy shell scripts under `scripts/`. Because cli.js is the `bin` target, the hidden code runs every time an operator invokes the advertised CLI, with the ambient privileges of the user running the deploy tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
